primary_text_note: All 15 poems were read in full from the board's own 2027 anthology PDF, so every quotation in the unit was verified verbatim, including the in-copyright poems. No lesson reproduces an in-copyright poem at length; all quotations are short embedded phrases.

findings.claim: Every one of the 90 practice questions across all 15 lessons is labelled '20 marks — Single Poem Analysis' or '20 marks — Poetry Comparison'.
findings.truth: The poetry section is 40 marks in two parts: 15 marks on the specified poem printed on the paper, then 25 marks comparing it with a second anthology poem the candidate chooses. There is no 20-mark poetry question on this paper. Relabelled to 15 (single poem, the even-index questions) and 25 (comparison, the odd-index questions). The house ladders carry no mark numbers, so they stay proportionate as written.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md lines 364-384 (Section B, 40 marks, two questions, AO1/AO2/AO3, closed book); Eduqas 'Component 1 Section B: The Poetry Anthology' teaching guide (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/txnpqebt/component-1-section-b-the-poetry-anthology.pdf) p.4 gives the sample split as [15] and [25] with 20 and 40 minutes advised.

findings.claim: Match-question option for 'Sonnet 29': 'A devoted wife reflects on overwhelming love'.
findings.truth: The Sonnets from the Portuguese were written in secret during the courtship of 1845-46, before the elopement, and were published in 1850. The speaker is not a wife, and Sonnet 29 is not a calm reflection — it is a demand that an absent lover replace her thoughts of him. Lesson 4 of this unit states the courtship facts correctly, so the two lessons contradicted each other.
findings.evidence: Sonnets from the Portuguese (1850); poem text in Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) p.13.

findings.claim: 'Owen uses para-rhyme — near-rhymes like “hymn” and “him” — instead of full rhyme.' Repeated in flashcard 11 and in the mark scheme for practice question 3.
findings.truth: 'Hymn' and 'him' are homophones, so they are an identical rhyme, not a near-rhyme. The example directly contradicts the lesson's own glossary definition of para-rhyme ('final consonant sounds match but the vowel sounds differ'). 'Disabled' in fact rhymes fully but with no fixed scheme, leaving lines such as 'hands' and the closing 'come' unmatched. The <dfn> and the glossary entry are kept; the claim now credits Owen's para-rhyme to his other war poems and describes the hymn/him pairing accurately.
findings.evidence: Poem text in Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) pp.16-18; line-end words dark/grey/park/hymn/day/him, then trees/knees/disease and dim/slim, are full rhymes in an irregular order.

findings.claim: 'a shorter second stanza beginning “Still I am fighting / You off”'.
findings.truth: The second stanza of 'Catrin' opens 'Neither won nor lost the struggle'. 'Still I am fighting / You off' is three lines into that stanza. A candidate quoting the wrong opening line would lose AO2 credit for a structural point.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) pp.22-23: stanza 1 ends 'To be two, to be ourselves.'; stanza 2 opens 'Neither won nor lost the struggle'.

findings.claim: Flashcard 8 asks 'What technique links ideas across the poem's single stanza?', and the mark scheme for practice question 2 praises Clarke's 'unbroken structure'.
findings.truth: 'Catrin' has two stanzas (17 lines, then 12), as the same lesson states twice elsewhere. Both places now say two stanzas or drop the single-stanza framing.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) pp.22-23.

findings.claim: 'the reader hears the story third-hand' in the opening paragraph, but 'we, the readers, receive it fourth-hand' in the Key Fact five lines later.
findings.truth: The two statements contradict each other, and neither is right. The narrator is the pilot's daughter — she calls his father 'grandfather's boat' and his wife 'my mother' — so her telling reaches the reader at second hand. Both places now say second-hand.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) pp.26-28: '– yes, grandfather's boat – safe' and 'my mother never spoke again / in his presence'.

findings.claim: The repo spec file's Appendix B lists an anthology of 18 poems (The Manhunt, Sonnet 43, London, The Soldier, She Walks in Beauty, Living Space, As Imperceptibly as Grief, Cozy Apologia, Valentine, A Wife in London, Death of a Naturalist, Hawk Roosting, To Autumn, Afternoons, Dulce et Decorum Est, Ozymandias, Mametz Wood, Excerpt from The Prelude). None of them is in this unit.
findings.truth: The unit is correct and the repo spec file is stale. The board replaced the anthology for first assessment in summer 2027 with a 15-poem set. The unit's 15 lessons match the new anthology exactly, in the anthology's own order, with the right poet for every poem. The repo copy of the spec is the 2015 edition (footer 'for teaching from 2015 / ED 24-10-14'), so it still carries the old list. Refresh specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md before the next checker runs, or a future pass will wrongly condemn the whole unit.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) pp.5-36 (contents page and poems); board announcement https://www.eduqas.co.uk/articles/enhancing-diversity-new-poetry-anthology-launched/ (15 poems, first assessed summer 2027).

findings.claim: Zulfikar Ghose 'grew up in colonial India before settling in Britain and later the United States'.
findings.truth: True as far as it goes, but it drops the fact that sharpens the poem's outsider stance. Ghose was born in Sialkot, Punjab, in 1935, into a Muslim family; the family moved to Bombay in 1942 and emigrated to England after Partition. Sialkot is now in Pakistan, so he is normally described as Pakistani-British or Pakistani-American. He died in Austin, Texas, in 2022. Nothing stated is wrong, so no edit.

findings.claim: Flashcard 5 calls 'We want, we shouted, to be two, to be ourselves' 'the daughter's cry for independence at birth'.
findings.truth: The poem's 'we' is mutual, and the lesson's own analysis says so: 'both mother and daughter want independence from each other'. Attributing the line to the daughter alone narrows it. Too small to edit.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) p.22.

findings.claim: 'her tone is far more anxious than Browning's calm confidence'.
findings.truth: Sonnet 29 is not calm — it uses imperatives and 'burst, shattered, everywhere!', as lesson 4 correctly says. The claim only works if it means the security of Browning's relationship rather than the poem's tone. Defensible enough to leave, but it reads oddly beside lesson 4.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) p.13.

findings.claim: 'he sees fishing boats lined up along the shore like decorations'.
findings.truth: The boats are on the open water beneath him, half way to the target: 'the little fishing boats / strung out like bunting / on a green-blue translucent sea'. 'Along the shore' misplaces them. Minor; no edit.
findings.evidence: Eduqas GCSE English Literature Poetry Anthology, for first assessment 2027 (https://www.eduqas.co.uk/media/szolurrz/new-poetry-anthology-for-first-examination-in-2027-mlp-18pt.pdf) p.26.

summary: Every lesson carries the same HIGH labelling error: 90 practice questions marked '20 marks' when the poetry section is 15 + 25. Five smaller factual fixes follow (Sonnet 29 called a wife's poem, hymn/him mislabelled as para-rhyme, two wrong structural claims about 'Catrin', and a self-contradicting narration distance in 'Kamikaze'). Quotations, poet dates, publication dates, forms, rhyme schemes and context claims are otherwise accurate, and no lesson names the board. One process note: the repo's spec markdown still lists the retired 18-poem anthology, while the unit correctly teaches the 15-poem anthology first assessed in 2027.
